text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- The Tocsik commission's draft report on last year's privatization scandal was rejected by a vote of 6-4, with all coalition members on the commission voting against it.
- The percentage of Hungarians supporting the country's future NATO membership has risen to 61 percent of the population from 47 percent in March.
- Four opposition parties attended a meeting initiated by Young Democrat (Fidesz) group leader Jozsef Szajer Wednesday to elaborate a national defense charter proposed by his party.
- The chairman of Parliament's national security committee said Wednesday that the so-called Operation Birch Tree was legal.

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn and Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima held talks on a special train carriage from Pamhagen to Sopron Wednesday on the 125th anniversary of the Gyor-Sopron-Ebenfurt Railway Rt.

- The chairman of the defense committee of the Russian Duma told Speaker of Parliament Zoltan Gal in Budapest yesterday that Hungary's invitation to join NATO does not fill Moscow with particular concern.
- President Arpad Goncz Wednesday told the U.N. General Assembly that progress on environmental protection considerations must be based on globalization, integration and mutual dependence.
- The cabinet today is expected to debate a proposal for the 1998 budget guidelines, according to which the central budget deficit will total Ft 430 billion, 4.7 percent of the GDP.

- The IMF delegation which left the country yesterday objected only to the excessive increase in the social security deficit, and concluded that Hungary's development renders further loan agreements unnecessary.
- The National Radio and Television Board (ORTT) Wednesday failed to award concessions for commercial television broadcasting to any of the three bidding consortia.

- The Canadian pharmaceutical company Novopharm has sued the State Privatization & Holding Co. (APV Rt.) regarding alleged violations of its pre-emptive right of subscription to shares in Human Rt., of which Novopharm owns 55 percent.
- The industrial vehicle manufacturer Raba Rt. has received an order for an annual $10-12 million in truck undercarriages from South Korean industrial giant Daewoo.
- The consortium Humex-Illit and representatives of the Industry and Trade Ministry yesterday signed a concession contract on mining gold and silver near Fuzerradvany, northeast Hungary.

- The directors of the State Privatization & Holding Co. (APV Rt.) yesterday announced that a 83 percent package in the oil drilling company Koolajkutato Rt. will go to MN Petroleum Services, of Oman.
- Privatization Minister Judit Csiha will present three options concerning the future of the bus maker Ikarus Rt. to the government at the cabinet's weekly meeting today.
- The public share offering of the dairy company Szabolcstej Rt. closed fully subscribed yesterday the State Privatisation & Holding Co. announced.
- The Budapest stock index reached a record high for the second straight day yesterday, closing at 6,779.59, an increase of 2.76 percent.
- A shoot-out broke out near Nyugati railway station shortly after 7 p.m. last night when a gunman fired shots into a bar's outdoor patio at 51 Terez krt.

- Police patrolling Nyugati ter in downtown Budapest yesterday afternoon seized two Yugoslav hand grenades, a Scorpion automatic pistol and matching ammunition and silencer as two men were about to make a deal.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Farmers plan to hold demonstrations in eight counties Friday against a planned amendment of the land law which would allow foreigners to purchase cropland in Hungary.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Parliament's defense committee has decided to set up an ad hoc investigative commission to probe details of the Kalashnikov affair.
- The Vienna-based electronic components producer Neutronics GmbH, owned by Philips, will invest another Ft 5 billion in its industrial park at Sarvar, western Hungary.
- The State Privatization & Holding Co. (APV Rt.) could be succeeded by two separate state-owned organizations, one for privatization, the other to manage state-owned property.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Berlin's prosecutor general Dieter Neumann yesterday vented his frustration with the Hungarian authorities' refusal to provide information related to the notorious terrorist Carlos the Jackal.
